messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — we received DSAR #2026-042. Request: full deletion of user artifacts, plus cryptographic proof that any derived embeddings were removed. They also asked whether we rotate/customer‑managed key material used for that tenant.
aj: Do we have a standard proof-of-deletion artifact for embeddings? I thought we return a deletion receipt but not a crypto attestation.
privacy-ops: For DSARs we usually: 1) identify all PII buckets, 2) delete primary records, 3) remove embeddings and indexes, 4) issue a deletion ticket with audit log links. Customer asking for key rotation is unusual but possible.
samir: Two gaps to highlight: audit log access is sampled for performance — we don't always keep full query payloads. Also, the logging agent had a bug in feb where snippet redaction wasn't applied to an intermediate buffer (tracked in #INC-2026-11).
cleo: Related RBAC ask — privacy team needs read access to raw audit logs for the proof. Current policy denies that; they'd need a scoped role and just-in-time access audit.
maria.g: Ok. Proposal: 1) Do a targeted key rotation for the tenant's KMS key and emit the rotation event. 2) Run a one-off audit export at full fidelity for the DSAR window (no sampling) into a KMS-encrypted export bucket. 3) Grant privacy-ops a scoped role with time-bound access (24h). 4) Produce a deletion report and include SHA256 hashes of deleted objects and the export manifest. Thoughts?
aj: I like the scoped role + time bound access. For step 2 we need to ensure logs we export don't include unrelated tenants. Filter by tenant_id before exporting. Also check quota for non-sampled export.
samir: About the rotation: rotating the key doesn't retroactively prove deletion of ciphertext that was already backed up unless we re-encrypt/export with new key and then delete old ciphertext. We can: a) rewrap objects with new key and then delete old versions, b) rotate and delete older wrapped versions if present. Both operations require careful coordination with KMS and S3-like lifecycle.
privacy-ops: Customer specifically asked we "rotate the key used to encrypt their embeddings and provide a signed statement of deletion." They also requested timestamps and audit links. If we can include the export manifest + rotation event (kms.key.version=3) plus hashes, that should satisfy legal.
cleo: On RBAC: ops-oncall or an automation service should perform the export to avoid exposing secrets. Can we use a temporary service account with only read-logs + write-export permissions and record the whole runbook in the ticket?
ops-oncall: I can run the export. Suggest using a GCS export (encrypted by the tenant KMS key) and then re-encrypt with a freshly created rotation key before handing the manifest to privacy-ops. I'll need the exact filters.
aj: Filters: time range = 2025-08-01 -> 2026-02-28, service tags = inference-api, indexer, embeddings-service; fields = request_id, tenant_id, callsite, token_approx, payload_hash (redact payload unless it's the one we export to the bucket).
samir: Also we need to ensure vuln triage note: if export includes raw prompts we must scrub any secrets (API keys, credentials) — add a scrub step using our redaction pipeline. Remember the feb bug — check if that affected the scrubbing library.
maria.g: Good call. samir, can you confirm the scrubbing lib version and whether the fix is in prod? If not, we run scrubbing in a hermetic container so we don't rely on prod agent.
samir: Current prod has 2.1.0 which is the vulnerable one. The fix is in 2.1.3. I'll build a hermetic container with 2.1.3 and run scrubbing as part of export pipeline.
cleo: For cryptographic proof, I'd prefer we include: - export manifest (file list + SHA256) - KMS rotation event log (key version create) - signed statement by security lead (PGP or our internal signing) - deletion ticket id and lifecycle deletion ops (object delete markers)
privacy-ops: That will be acceptable. Legal wants the signed statement to reference the ticket and the export manifest checksum.
ops-oncall: Ops runbook (draft): 1) Create rotation key: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=tenant-xyz-key --location=global --keyring=rotations` 2) Export filtered logs to gs://redwood-dsar-exports/tenant-xyz/2026-03-05/ 3) Run hermetic scrubbing container: `docker run --rm -e INPUT=... redwood/scrub:2.1.3` 4) Rewrap export objects with new rotation key and delete old wrapped blobs. 5) Upload manifest + sig to secure evidence bucket.
maria.g: Perfect. Who owns creating the short-lived role for privacy-ops?
cleo: I can create an IAM role `privates/dsar_viewer` with `auditlogs.viewer` and `storage.objects.get` scoped to that export bucket, then grant it for 24h. I will add a policy binding and record it.
aj: One more: retention exception. If we delete embeddings now we must log a retention-exception event if the data would otherwise be subject to retention policy (e.g., search-training-index). Privacy will need the exception recorded so we don't auto-recreate from backups.
privacy-ops: We'll file retention-exception REF-2026-114 and include approval chain. Good call.
samir: Also mark this flow in vuln-triage as "sensitive export" — require two-person review before any plaintext leaves environment.
maria.g: Action items: * samir: build hermetic scrub container and confirm redaction fix in 2.1.3 (ETA 6h). * ops-oncall: execute export + rewrap (ETA 12h after scrub confirmed). * cleo: create short-lived IAM role (before export). * privacy-ops: prepare deletion statement template and legal text. * aj: add retention-exception ticket and link. We'll sync here once export completes.
privacy-ops: Thanks — keeping customer updated. Please ping me when the signed manifest is ready so I can attach to the DSAR response. :white_check_mark:
devops-bot: Incident #INC-2026-11 was referenced — follow-up note added to ticket DSAR-2026-042.
